title: RobCo Valuation Doubles to $1B in Secondary Sale
summary:
Venture capital firms including Sequoia and Cherry Ventures have acquired shares in a Munich-based industrial automation firm. RobCo sold $40M of shares in a secondary transaction that valued the company at more than $1B, which is double the approximately $500M valuation it held after raising $100M in January. The deal highlights growing investor appetite for physical AI systems that can automate unstructured manual tasks.

Founded in 2020 by Roman Hölzl, the company develops the Alfie robot, which is designed for safety-critical work on factory floors. The startup is scheduled to put its first robot on sale early next year. Participating investors in the current round include existing backers Lightspeed, Greenfield, Kindred and Lingotto.

Europe has JUST got another robotics unicorn!

LETS GO

The German company builds autonomous industrial robots. 

Its main one is called Alfie - a purpose-built robot for the autonomous industrial lifecycle that can perform a range of unstructured, safety-critical work on factory floors.

It was founded in 2020 by @romanhoelzl and its first robot will go on sale early next year.

Today, it is announced to be running a secondary sale at a $1 billion+ valuation. 

Existing investors including Sequoia, Lightspeed, Greenfield, Kindred and Lingotto are taking part, as well as new investors @CherryVentures.

I love seeing secondary sales and I love seeing Europe get more deep tech unicorns. This is a DOUBLE WIN WIN ON A MONDAY MORNING.

Huge congrats to the @Robco_Robotics team!
